prerequisites: Competencies taught in the modules Object-Oriented Programming and Algorithms and Data Structures are recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: have basic skills in data modeling
know techniques for implementing data models in a database design
have insights into important query calculi
know beyond the basic functionality of SQL
know the basics of transaction management
can practically handle database management systems
are able to apply scientific working methods in independently recognizing, formulating and solving problems
are able to speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion

syllabus_topics: Methods and tools of data modeling

assessment_methods.method: Oral presentation of solutions to at least two exercises

assessment_rules: To acquire credit points, at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercises must be achieved, and the solution of at least two exercises must be presented orally. Grading is done with 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the B.Sc. Business Informatics degree program. A resit exam is possible.
bibliography: Heuer, G. Saake: "Datenbanken: Konzepte und Sprachen", Thomson.
G. Saake, Kai-Uwe Sattler: "Datenbanken und Java. JDBC, SQLJ und ODMG", dpunkt Verlag.
